abilities._comment: Optional additional cost: you MAY destroy a Gold you control; if you do, this gets +3{p} and overpower. Only offered when you control a Gold; option 0 destroys + buffs, option 1 declines.

_comment:
'Victor Specialization. As an additional cost to play this, you MAY destroy a Gold you control. If you do, this gets +3{p} and OVERPOWER. When you win a clash revealing this, create a Gold token.'

The choice was modelled correctly -- CHOOSE offers destroy-and-buff or decline, and is only offered while you control a Gold -- but the printed Overpower applied unconditionally, so a player who kept their Gold got the overpower anyway and the trade the card asks for was free.

The keyword is DECLARED conditional rather than converted to a WHILE_STATIC: "if you DO" is about a choice made at resolution, not a state a static could re-read.
